records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֗ה ע֣וֹד נֶ֤גַע אֶחָד֙ אָבִ֤יא עַל־פַּרְעֹה֙ וְעַל־מִצְרַ֔יִם אַֽחֲרֵי־כֵ֕ן יְשַׁלַּ֥ח אֶתְכֶ֖ם מִזֶּ֑ה כְּשַׁ֨לְּח֔וֹ כָּלָ֕ה גָּרֵ֛שׁ יְגָרֵ֥שׁ אֶתְכֶ֖ם מִזֶּֽה׃
records.gloss: And said Yahweh to Moses, yet one plague I will bring on Pharaoh and on Egypt; after that he will let go you from here. When he lets [you] go, completely he will surely drive out you from here.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "There is one plague still to come. I will bring it on Pharaoh and on Egypt, and after it he will let you leave this place. When he lets you go, he will drive you out of here for good.

L.1: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Yet one plague I will bring upon Pharaoh and upon Egypt; after that he will let you go from here. When he lets [you] go, completely, he will surely drive you out from here.

R.1: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "I will send one last disaster on Pharaoh and on Egypt. After that, Pharaoh will let you go. In fact, when he lets you go, he will chase you out of the land.

decisions.choice: said: the telling of a word God gave Moses, perhaps earlier
decisions.reason: Moses is still standing before Pharaoh: he began speaking in 10:29 and goes out from Pharaoh only in verse 8. So verses 1-3 may tell what God had said to Moses before this meeting ("had said"), set here to explain what Moses announces in verses 4-8. The verb form allows either reading.

decisions.choice: plague: a blow, a stroke
decisions.reason: The word means a blow or stroke, often one sent by God. "One more" marks this as the last of the plagues: the death of the firstborn (verses 4-7; 12:29).

decisions.choice: completely: going with "drive out" (he will drive you out altogether)
alternatives: when he lets you go for good, he will drive you out
decisions.reason: The word "completely" stands between the two verbs. It may describe the driving out (Pharaoh will drive Israel out once and for all, every one of them) or the letting go (when he lets you go for good, he will drive you out). Either way Pharaoh will not only allow Israel to leave but force them out, as 12:31-33 tells.

decisions.choice: Pharaoh ... In fact ... out of the land
decisions.reason: Readable names Pharaoh as the subject and says "the land" for "here", meaning Egypt. "Last" renders "yet one": there will be no more after it.

records.heading: One plague still to come

records.source: דַּבֶּר־נָ֖א בְּאָזְנֵ֣י הָעָ֑ם וְיִשְׁאֲל֞וּ אִ֣ישׁ׀מֵאֵ֣ת רֵעֵ֗הוּ וְאִשָּׁה֙ מֵאֵ֣ת רְעוּתָ֔הּ כְּלֵי־כֶ֖סֶף וּכְלֵ֥י זָהָֽב׃
records.gloss: Speak please in [the] ears of the people, that they may ask, each man from with his neighbor and each woman from with her neighbor, articles of silver and articles of gold.
pieces: Now tell the people, so that all of them hear it, that each man is to ask his Egyptian neighbor, and each woman hers, for articles of silver and gold."

L.2: Speak, please, in the ears of the people, that they ask, each man of his neighbor and each woman of her neighbor, articles of silver and articles of gold."

R.2: Tell the people that every man and every woman should ask their Egyptian neighbors for things made of silver and gold."

decisions.choice: speak in the ears of the people: tell them plainly, so all can hear
decisions.reason: The phrase means to speak directly and clearly to a group, so that they all hear (Genesis 50:4; Exodus 24:7).

decisions.choice: ask: request, and receive as a gift
decisions.reason: The same verb as in 3:22, where God first said the Israelites would ask the Egyptians for silver and gold. It is a request, not a loan to be paid back. What is promised here is done in 12:35-36.

decisions.choice: each man ... each woman: the whole people
decisions.reason: In 3:22 only the women were told to ask. Here men and women both are.

decisions.choice: Egyptian neighbor
decisions.reason: The neighbors are Egyptians, as the next verse shows, so Balanced and Readable say so, as in 3:22. Literal keeps "his neighbor" and "her neighbor".

records.source: וַיִּתֵּ֧ן יְהוָ֛ה אֶת־חֵ֥ן הָעָ֖ם בְּעֵינֵ֣י מִצְרָ֑יִם גַּ֣ם׀הָאִ֣ישׁ מֹשֶׁ֗ה גָּד֤וֹל מְאֹד֙ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם בְּעֵינֵ֥י עַבְדֵֽי־פַרְעֹ֖ה וּבְעֵינֵ֥י הָעָֽם׃ס
records.gloss: And gave Yahweh [the] favor of the people in [the] eyes of Egypt. Also the man Moses [was] very great in [the] land of Egypt, in [the] eyes of [the] servants of Pharaoh and in [the] eyes of the people.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} made the Egyptians look kindly on the people. Moses, too, was a very great man in the land of Egypt; Pharaoh's officials and the people looked on him with respect.

L.3: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave the people favor in the eyes of the Egyptians. Also the man Moses [was] very great in the land of Egypt, in the eyes of Pharaoh's servants and in the eyes of the people.

R.3: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} made the Egyptians friendly toward the Israelites. And Moses had become a very important man in Egypt. Pharaoh's officials and the people respected him greatly.

decisions.choice: Yahweh gave the people favor: the promise of 3:21 is kept
decisions.reason: In 3:21 God said, "I will give this people favor in the eyes of the Egyptians." The narrator now says that he has done so, which is why the Egyptians will give what is asked (12:36).

decisions.choice: the people: most likely the Egyptian people
decisions.reason: Set beside "Pharaoh's servants", "the people" here most likely means the Egyptians at large, not Israel, who is "the people" earlier in the verse. Moses was honored by the court and by ordinary Egyptians alike.

decisions.choice: officials
decisions.reason: Pharaoh's "servants" are his court and officials (5:21; 8:5). Literal keeps "servants".

decisions.choice: the Israelites
decisions.reason: The first "the people" is Israel; Readable names them.

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֔ה כֹּ֖ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה כַּחֲצֹ֣ת הַלַּ֔יְלָה אֲנִ֥י יוֹצֵ֖א בְּת֥וֹךְ מִצְרָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: And said Moses, thus says Yahweh: about [the] middle of the night I [am] going out in [the] midst of Egypt.
pieces: Moses then told Pharaoh, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} says this: 'Around midnight I am going out into the heart of Egypt.

L.4: And Moses said, "Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: 'About the middle of the night I am going out into the midst of Egypt.

R.4: Moses told Pharaoh, "Here is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: 'Around midnight I will go out among the people of Egypt.

decisions.choice: about midnight: around the middle of a coming night
decisions.reason: "About" marks a time of night, not an exact hour, and the verse does not say which night. Chapter 12 sets it: the night of the Passover, when it happened "in the middle of the night" (12:29).

decisions.choice: I am going out: God himself acts
decisions.reason: The word "I" is stressed. This last plague is not brought by Aaron's staff or Moses' hand, as the others were; God himself goes out through Egypt (12:12, 23).

decisions.choice: told Pharaoh
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "Moses said". He is still speaking to Pharaoh, whom he leaves in verse 8, so Balanced and Readable name him.

records.heading: Moses warns of the death of the firstborn

records.source: וּמֵ֣ת כָּל־בְּכוֹר֮ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַיִם֒ מִבְּכ֤וֹר פַּרְעֹה֙ הַיֹּשֵׁ֣ב עַל־כִּסְא֔וֹ עַ֚ד בְּכ֣וֹר הַשִּׁפְחָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֖ר אַחַ֣ר הָרֵחָ֑יִם וְכֹ֖ל בְּכ֥וֹר בְּהֵמָֽה׃
records.gloss: And will die every firstborn in [the] land of Egypt, from [the] firstborn of Pharaoh who sits on his throne to [the] firstborn of the slave woman who [is] behind the millstones, and every firstborn of livestock.
pieces: Every firstborn in the land of Egypt will die, from the firstborn of Pharaoh, seated on his throne, to the firstborn of the female servant who grinds grain at the millstones, and every firstborn of the animals as well.

L.5: And every firstborn in the land of Egypt will die, from the firstborn of Pharaoh who sits on his throne to the firstborn of the slave woman who [is] behind the millstones, and every firstborn of [the] livestock.

R.5: Every oldest son in Egypt will die. The oldest son of Pharaoh, who rules from his throne, will die. So will the oldest son of the servant woman who grinds grain by hand. The firstborn males of the animals will die too.

decisions.choice: firstborn: the eldest son, and the first male born to an animal
decisions.reason: The firstborn is the first son born to a father or mother, who held the first place in the family. God called Israel "my firstborn son" and warned Pharaoh, "I will kill your firstborn son" (4:22-23). Among animals the firstborn is the first male born (13:12, 15).

decisions.choice: the slave woman behind the millstones: the lowest worker in the land
decisions.reason: Grain was ground into flour by hand between two stones, hard daily work done by slave women and captives (Judges 16:21; Isaiah 47:2). From Pharaoh on his throne to the slave at the mill means everyone, from the highest to the lowest.

decisions.choice: oldest son ... firstborn males of the animals
decisions.reason: Readable says "oldest son" for people, as in 4:23, and spells out that the firstborn of animals are the males.

decisions.choice: female servant; servant woman
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable (style guide); Literal keeps "slave". The meaning decision (m2) keeps that she is the lowest worker in the land.

records.source: וְהָֽיְתָ֛ה צְעָקָ֥ה גְדֹלָ֖ה בְּכָל־אֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם אֲשֶׁ֤ר כָּמֹ֨הוּ֙ לֹ֣א נִהְיָ֔תָה וְכָמֹ֖הוּ לֹ֥א תֹסִֽף׃
records.gloss: And there will be a great cry in all [the] land of Egypt, which like it there has not been, and like it [there] will not be again.
pieces: A great cry of grief will go up across the whole land of Egypt. Nothing like it has happened before, and nothing like it will happen again.

L.6: And there will be a great cry in all the land of Egypt, the like of which has not been, and the like of which will not be again.

R.6: People all over Egypt will cry out loudly in sorrow. There has never been crying like it, and there never will be again.

decisions.choice: a great cry: the same word as Israel's cry in their slavery
decisions.reason: God heard "the cry" of the Israelites under their slave drivers (3:7, 9). Now the cry will be Egypt's. It is fulfilled in 12:30.

decisions.choice: such as has not been and will not be again: without equal
decisions.reason: The same kind of phrase is used of the hail (9:18, 24) and the locusts (10:6, 14). Here it marks the worst grief Egypt will ever know.

decisions.choice: cry of grief / in sorrow
decisions.reason: The cry is one of mourning for the dead (12:30). Balanced and Readable say so; Literal keeps "cry".

records.source: וּלְכֹ֣ל׀בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל לֹ֤א יֶֽחֱרַץ־כֶּ֨לֶב֙ לְשֹׁנ֔וֹ לְמֵאִ֖ישׁ וְעַד־בְּהֵמָ֑ה לְמַ֨עַן֙ תֵּֽדְע֔וּן אֲשֶׁר֙ יַפְלֶ֣ה יְהוָ֔ה בֵּ֥ין מִצְרַ֖יִם וּבֵ֥ין יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: But against all [the] sons of Israel not will sharpen a dog its tongue, from man and to beast, so that you may know that distinguishes Yahweh between Egypt and between Israel.
pieces: But among the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} not even a dog will snarl at anyone, human or animal. So you will know that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} sets Israel apart from Egypt.'

L.7: But against any of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel not a dog will sharpen its tongue, against man or beast, so that you may know that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} distinguishes between Egypt and Israel.'

R.7: But not even a dog will growl at any of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} or their animals. Then you will know that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} treats the Egyptians and the Israelites differently.'

decisions.choice: not a dog will sharpen its tongue: not even a dog will growl
decisions.reason: A dog that sharpens its tongue snarls or barks to threaten. The picture is of complete calm: while Egypt cries out, nothing will so much as growl at Israel (compare Joshua 10:21).

decisions.choice: distinguishes: sets apart, treats differently
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used of setting Goshen apart in 8:18 and Israel's livestock in 9:4.

decisions.choice: the words of Yahweh end here
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has no quotation marks. Moses quotes God from verse 4, and the change to "Yahweh" here and to Moses' own "me" in verse 8 suggests God's words end with this verse, or perhaps with verse 6. In verse 8 Moses speaks for himself.

decisions.choice: sets ... apart / treats ... differently
decisions.reason: Balanced says that the LORD "sets Israel apart", as in 8:18 and 9:4; Readable says he "treats" them "differently".

records.source: וְיָרְד֣וּ כָל־עֲבָדֶיךָ֩ אֵ֨לֶּה אֵלַ֜י וְהִשְׁתַּֽחֲוּוּ־לִ֣ילֵאמֹ֗ר צֵ֤א אַתָּה֙ וְכָל־הָעָ֣ם אֲשֶׁר־בְּרַגְלֶ֔יךָ וְאַחֲרֵי־כֵ֖ן אֵצֵ֑א וַיֵּצֵ֥א מֵֽעִם־פַּרְעֹ֖ה בָּחֳרִי־אָֽף׃ס
records.gloss: And will come down all these your servants to me and bow down to me, saying, go out, you and all the people who [are] at your feet. And after that I will go out. And he went out from with Pharaoh in heat of anger.
pieces: Every one of these officials of yours will come down to me and bow to the ground, and they will say, 'Leave, you and all the people at your heels!' Only then will I go." And Moses walked out from Pharaoh's presence in fierce anger.

L.8: And all these servants of yours will come down to me and bow down to me, saying, 'Go out, you and all the people who [are] at your feet.' And after that I will go out." And he went out from Pharaoh in heat of anger.

R.8: All these officials of yours will come to me and bow down to the ground. They will beg me to leave, along with all the people who follow me. After that, I will go." Then Moses left Pharaoh. He was very angry.

decisions.choice: your servants will bow down to me and say "Go out": Pharaoh's court will beg Israel to leave
decisions.reason: Pharaoh had sent Moses away and threatened him with death (10:28). Now Moses says Pharaoh's own officials will bow before him and urge him to go. In 12:31-33 Pharaoh and the Egyptians send Israel out in haste.

decisions.choice: the people at your feet: the people who follow you
decisions.reason: To be "at the feet" of a leader is to follow him (Judges 4:10; 8:5).

decisions.choice: in heat of anger: burning with anger
decisions.reason: The phrase describes fierce anger. Moses leaves angry at Pharaoh's refusal and his threat (10:28-29).

decisions.choice: Moses
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "he went out"; Balanced and Readable name Moses, who has been speaking. Readable also turns the officials' words into reported speech.

records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֔ה לֹא־יִשְׁמַ֥ע אֲלֵיכֶ֖ם פַּרְעֹ֑ה לְמַ֛עַן רְב֥וֹת מוֹפְתַ֖י בְּאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: And said Yahweh to Moses, not will listen to you Pharaoh, so as to be many my wonders in [the] land of Egypt.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Pharaoh will not heed you, so that I may do still more wonders in the land of Egypt."

L.9: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Pharaoh will not listen to you, in order that {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} wonders may increase in the land of Egypt."

R.9: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Pharaoh will not listen to you. So I will do even more wonders in the land of Egypt."

decisions.choice: Pharaoh will not listen ... my wonders: a summary of 7:3-4
decisions.reason: Verses 9-10 close the account of the plagues that began in 7:3-4, where God said Pharaoh would not listen and he would multiply his signs and wonders. "Said" may here mean "had said", looking back to that word.

decisions.choice: so that my wonders may be many: God's purpose in Pharaoh's refusal
decisions.reason: Pharaoh's refusal does not defeat God's plan; it gives occasion for more of his wonders, so that Egypt and Israel would know who he is (7:5; 10:2).

records.source: וּמֹשֶׁ֣ה וְאַהֲרֹ֗ן עָשׂ֛וּ אֶת־כָּל־הַמֹּפְתִ֥ים הָאֵ֖לֶּה לִפְנֵ֣י פַרְעֹ֑ה וַיְחַזֵּ֤ק יְהוָה֙ אֶת־לֵ֣ב פַּרְעֹ֔ה וְלֹֽא־שִׁלַּ֥ח אֶת־בְּנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל מֵאַרְצֽוֹ׃פ
records.gloss: And Moses and Aaron did all the these wonders before Pharaoh, and made strong Yahweh [the] heart of Pharaoh, and not he let go [the] sons of Israel from his land.
pieces: Moses and Aaron did all these wonders in front of Pharaoh, but {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} made Pharaoh's heart stubborn, and he did not release the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} from his land.

L.10: And Moses and Aaron did all these wonders before Pharaoh, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} made Pharaoh's heart strong, and he did not let the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel go from his land.

R.10: Moses and Aaron did all these wonders in front of Pharaoh. But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} made Pharaoh stubborn, and he would not let the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} leave his country.

decisions.choice: Yahweh made Pharaoh's heart strong: God confirmed Pharaoh in his resistance
decisions.reason: The verb means to make firm or strong, as in 4:21, 9:12 and 10:20. Pharaoh had also made his own heart heavy (8:11, 28). See the note at 7:3.

decisions.choice: these wonders: the plagues of chapters 7-10
decisions.reason: The wonders done before Pharaoh are the signs God promised in 4:21 and 7:3. The last one, announced in verses 4-7, is still to come.

decisions.choice: made Pharaoh's heart stubborn (Balanced); made Pharaoh stubborn (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in 4:21 and 7:3. Literal keeps "made Pharaoh's heart strong".
